problems.name: Valid Anagram
problems.question: Given two strings s and t, return true if t is an anagram of s and false otherwise.
problems.constraints: 1 <= s.length, t.length <= 50000; s and t contain lowercase English letters.

examples.explanation: Both strings contain the same characters with the same counts.
The character counts differ.
Different lengths cannot be anagrams.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(1). Count 26 lowercase letters.

problems.name: Valid Palindrome
problems.question: Given a string s, return true if it is a palindrome after converting uppercase letters to lowercase and removing non-alphanumeric characters.
problems.constraints: 1 <= s.length <= 200000; s consists of printable ASCII characters.

examples.input: s = "A man, a plan, a canal: Panama"
examples.explanation: Normalized string is amanaplanacanalpanama.
Normalized string is not symmetric.
No alphanumeric characters remain.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(1). Two pointers skip ignored characters in place.

problems.name: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
problems.question: Given a string s, return the length of the longest substring without repeating characters.
problems.constraints: 0 <= s.length <= 50000; s consists of English letters, digits, symbols, and spaces.

examples.explanation: The longest substrings include abc.
Only one repeated character can be used.
wke is valid; pwke is not contiguous.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(charset). Sliding window moves each boundary at most n times.

source.label: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters - LeetCode 3

problems.name: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
problems.question: Given a string s and integer k, return the length of the longest substring that can be made of one repeated character after at most k replacements.
problems.constraints: 1 <= s.length <= 100000; s contains uppercase English letters; 0 <= k <= s.length.

examples.explanation: Replace two letters to make the whole string equal.
AABA or ABBA can be made uniform.
No replacement is needed.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(1). Sliding window tracks 26 uppercase counts.

problems.name: Minimum Window Substring
problems.question: Given strings s and t, return the minimum window substring of s that contains every character of t including duplicates.
problems.constraints: 1 <= s.length, t.length <= 100000; s and t consist of uppercase and lowercase English letters.

examples.explanation: BANC is the smallest window containing A, B, and C.
The only character satisfies the requirement.
The source does not contain enough a characters.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(charset). Sliding window expands and contracts each index once.

problems.name: Group Anagrams
problems.question: Given an array of strings, group the anagrams together in any order.
problems.constraints: 1 <= strs.length <= 10000; 0 <= strs[i].length <= 100; strs[i] contains lowercase English letters.

examples.explanation: Words with the same sorted key are grouped.
The empty string forms one group.
One word forms one group.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(nL); Space O(nL). Use a 26-count signature as the map key.

problems.name: Encode and Decode Strings
problems.question: Design an algorithm to encode a list of strings into one string and decode it back to the original list.
problems.constraints: 0 <= strs.length <= 200; 0 <= strs[i].length <= 200; strings may contain any valid characters.

examples.explanation: Each length prefix makes decoding unambiguous.
Length zero is encoded explicitly.
Delimiter characters inside content are preserved.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Encode O(total characters); decode O(total characters); Space O(total characters). Length prefixes avoid escaping.

problems.name: Longest Palindromic Substring
problems.question: Given a string s, return the longest palindromic substring in s.
problems.constraints: 1 <= s.length <= 1000; s consists of digits and English letters.

examples.explanation: Both length-three palindromes are valid.
The longest palindrome has an even center.
A single character is a palindrome.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n^2); Space O(1). Expand around each center.

problems.name: Palindromic Substrings
problems.question: Given a string s, return the number of palindromic substrings in it.
problems.constraints: 1 <= s.length <= 1000; s consists of lowercase English letters.

examples.explanation: Only single-character palindromes exist.
Three singles, two aa substrings, and one aaa.
a, b, a, and aba are palindromes.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n^2); Space O(1). Expand around 2n-1 centers.

problems.name: Valid Parenthesis String
problems.question: Given a string containing (, ), and *, return true if * can be treated as (, ), or empty to make the string valid.
problems.constraints: 1 <= s.length <= 100; s[i] is (, ), or *.

examples.explanation: Already valid.
* can be empty.
* can be an opening parenthesis.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(1). Greedy lower and upper open-count bounds.

problems.name: Find the Index of the First Occurrence in a String
problems.question: Given strings haystack and needle, return the index of the first occurrence of needle in haystack, or -1 if it is not present.
problems.constraints: 1 <= haystack.length, needle.length <= 10000; strings contain lowercase English letters.

examples.explanation: The first occurrence starts at index 0.
The pattern is absent.
Repeated haystack characters still do not match.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n+m); Space O(m). KMP scans haystack once after prefix preprocessing.

source.label: Find the Index of the First Occurrence in a String - LeetCode 28

problems.name: Repeated Substring Pattern
problems.question: Given a string s, return true if it can be constructed by repeating one of its proper substrings multiple times.
problems.constraints: 1 <= s.length <= 10000; s consists of lowercase English letters.

examples.explanation: ab repeated twice forms the string.
No proper substring repeats to form it.
abc repeats four times.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(n). The prefix table gives the longest border; a valid period is n - border when it divides n.

problems.name: String Compression
problems.question: Given an array of characters, compress it in place by replacing each group with the character followed by its count when count is greater than one, and return the new length.
problems.constraints: 1 <= chars.length <= 2000; chars[i] is a lowercase/uppercase letter, digit, or symbol.

examples.explanation: Each repeated run writes its count.
A count of one is omitted.
Multi-digit counts are written one digit at a time.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(1). Two pointers read runs and write compressed output in place.

problems.name: Reverse Words in a String
problems.question: Given a string s, reverse the order of its words, removing leading/trailing spaces and reducing multiple spaces to one.
problems.constraints: 1 <= s.length <= 10000; s contains English letters, digits, and spaces.

examples.explanation: Word order is reversed.
Outer spaces are removed.
Multiple spaces collapse to one.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(n). Parse words from the end without storing all tokens first.

problems.name: Zigzag Conversion
problems.question: Given a string s and number of rows, write the string in zigzag order and then read row by row.
problems.constraints: 1 <= s.length <= 1000; 1 <= numRows <= 1000; s contains English letters, comma, and period.

examples.explanation: Rows are read after zigzag placement.
A different row count changes the cycle.
One row leaves the string unchanged.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(n). Append directly to row builders while simulating direction.

problems.name: Add Strings
problems.question: Given two non-negative integers as strings, return their sum as a string without converting the full inputs to integers.

examples.explanation: Carry propagates across digits.
Zero plus zero remains zero.

problems.name: Decode String
problems.question: Given an encoded string with patterns k[encoded_string], return the decoded string.

examples.explanation: Each bracketed block repeats independently.

problems.name: Basic Calculator II
problems.question: Given a string expression containing non-negative integers and operators +, -, *, /, evaluate it with integer division truncating toward zero.
problems.constraints: 1 <= s.length <= 300000; s consists of digits, spaces, +, -, *, and /; expression is valid.

examples.explanation: Multiplication happens before addition.
Integer division truncates toward zero.
5 / 2 becomes 2, then 3 + 2.

problems.name: Longest Common Prefix

examples.explanation: All strings share fl.

problems.name: Compare Version Numbers

examples.explanation: Leading zeros do not change segment value.
